get.summary:
`GET /collector/remotes` — list every remote. Gated by
[`Scoped<LiveRemotesReader>`] (`wildflower/Accounts.r`): a remote's `config`
can carry origin credentials, so even the listing requires the read scope. The
capability is the only door to the store — this handler never sees the state.

post.summary:
`POST /collector/remotes` — create a remote. Gated by
[`Scoped<LiveRemotesCreator>`] (`wildflower/Accounts.c`); the capability is the
only door to the store, so this handler never sees the state.

409.description: A remote with this id already exists

get.summary:
`GET /collector/remotes/{id}` — fetch one remote. Gated by
[`Scoped<LiveRemotesReader>`] (`wildflower/Accounts.r`); the scope check runs
during extraction, before this body, so an under-scoped caller gets a `403`
whether or not the id exists.

put.summary:
`PUT /collector/remotes/{id}` — replace a remote's name + config. Gated by
[`Scoped<LiveRemotesEditor>`] (`wildflower/Accounts.u`); the capability is the
only door to the store, so this handler never sees the state.

delete.summary:
`DELETE /collector/remotes/{id}` — remove a remote. Gated by
[`Scoped<LiveRemotesDeleter>`] (`wildflower/Accounts.d`); the capability is the
only door to the store, so this handler never sees the state.

CreateRemoteBody.description:
POST body — matches the TS `CreateRemotePayloadSchema`. `config` is the
tagged `CollectorConfig` JSON, opaque to Rust (see [`Remote::config`]) —
`value_type = Value` keeps its OpenAPI schema an unconstrained wildcard.

DeletedBody.description:
Wire shape for the delete acknowledgement — matches the TS success schema
(`Schema.Struct({ deleted: Schema.Boolean })`).

InsufficientScopeBody.description:
Wire shape for a 403 — the caller authenticated, but their token doesn't cover
the scope(s) an operation requires. `missingScopes` names the scopes the
caller must additionally hold.

error.description: Always `"InsufficientScope"` — the discriminant a client switches on.

missingScopes.description: The rendered scopes the caller lacks.

InvalidConfigBody.description:
Wire shape for a 400 `InvalidConfig` — the submitted config carries no
string `_tag`, so the denormalized `tag` column (and the wire `tag` field)
can't be produced. Matches the TS `InvalidConfigSchema`. Unreachable through
the typed TS client (which validates the config union before sending), but
modeled so a non-UI client gets a decodable failure.

Remote.description:
A stored remote — the wire shape the `/collector/remotes` endpoints serve
(the TS `RemoteSchema` in
`collector-registry/src/http-api-definition/remotes.ts`) AND the
`collector_remotes` row: the diesel derives map this type straight to/from
the table, with [`JsonText`] converting `config` between `Value` and the
JSON TEXT column at the bind/read boundary. serde's camelCase rename
produces the wire's `addedAt`.

tag.description:
Denormalized copy of `config._tag`, written alongside the config so
clients filtering by collector kind don't need to crack the config JSON
(mirrors the TS `RemoteSchema.tag` doc). Kept in sync by the write
handlers — [`config_tag`] is the single reader they both denormalize
through.

config.description:
The full tagged `CollectorConfig` JSON, **opaque to Rust**: the
per-collector config union is TS-owned (`collector-registry`'s registry),
so this crate stores and serves it verbatim rather than modeling it —
adding a TS collector never requires a Rust change. The column keeps
it as JSON TEXT; [`JsonText`] round-trips it through `serde_json`.
`value_type = Value` keeps the OpenAPI schema an unconstrained `{}` (a
wildcard to the TS spec-drift engine), matching that opacity.

addedAt.description:
ISO-8601 UTC with milliseconds (e.g. `2026-06-17T14:29:22.363Z`) —
the encoding the TS `Schema.DateTimeUtc` round-trips.

RemoteAlreadyExistsBody.description:
Wire shape for a 409 `RemoteAlreadyExists` — a create with a client-minted
id that's already taken. Matches the TS `RemoteAlreadyExistsSchema`.

RemoteNotFoundBody.description: Wire shape for the 404. Matches the TS `RemoteNotFoundSchema`.

UpdateRemoteBody.description:
PUT body — matches the TS `UpdateRemotePayloadSchema`. Both fields are
required (a full replace, not a patch); `config` stays opaque to Rust.
